story: Bradley Lake, the Dixon Glacier diversion and the Railbelt's gas-short winter (S1), with the UA AI symposium and UAA NSF RAISE rural AI mini-grants as runner-up (S2)
notes: CONTRADICTIONS AND HOW TO PRINT THEM. (1) 38 vs 40 percent. The FERC notice in the Federal Register (primary) says the expansion raises average annual generation by 'approximately 38 percent'. AEA's July 20th release gives +167,000 MWh on a current 436,000 MWh, rising to 603,000 MWh, which works out to 38.3 percent, yet the same release calls it 'more than 40 percent'. The July 23rd release says 'approximately 40 percent'. KTUU says 'increasing water capacity by 40%', which is water, not energy. 167,000 over the 1995-2020 average of 392,000 MWh is 42.6 percent, which probably explains AEA's 40-plus figure. Print 'about 38 percent more electricity a year, per the FERC notice' and keep 40 percent only as KTUU's water-capacity figure. (2) 120 vs 119.7 MW. AEA and KTUU say 120 MW. FERC says installed capacity goes from 119.7 MW to 120.0 MW with the 0.3 MW micro-turbine. Print 'about 120 MW' for today. The expansion adds energy, not capacity. (3) 392,000 vs 436,000 MWh are different measures. 392,000 is AEA's 1995-2020 average and 436,000 is AEA's 'currently generates' figure. Never present them as one number. (4) Fairbanks vs Interior diesel. The 250,000 gallons a day is Thayer's spoken quote, 'There's not enough natural gas to ship to Fairbanks. They are right now using 250,000 gallons of diesel a day.' KTUU's own narration says 'Interior utilities' are buying fuel from refineries but does not put the 250,000 figure in narration. Print it as Fairbanks, attributed to Thayer. (5) 600 vs nearly 700 miles. KTUU says the population stretches '600 miles from Homer north to Fairbanks'. The RRC says the utilities are 'interconnected across nearly 700 miles'. These are different measures, so do not mix them. (6) Tunnel. AEA (primary) says a 4.6-mile tunnel. KTUU says 'directionally drill five miles through a mountain'. The AEA Dixon page's 'five miles southwest of Bradley Lake' is a location, not the tunnel. Print 4.6 miles. (7) Timeline. The AEA Dixon page says three years of study and permitting, then three years of construction. The July 23rd release says construction is anticipated to begin in 2027. KTUU says completion is slated for 2030 and transmission for 2031 or 2032. These are consistent. Hedge the dates as expected. (8) KTUU dating. The URL path says 2026/09/25, but the page reads 'Published: Sep. 24, 2026 at 9:34 PM AKDT'. Use September 24th. (9) The brief's Thayer quote was misworded. The page reads 'We're going to have to turn off the lights and we're going to have to turn down the heat', not 'turn off the lights and turn down the heat'. (10) Air Force deadline. Air and Space Forces (April 11th) says proposals were due May 29, not June 29. A later extension was not verified. (11) PRIMARY sources reached: Federal Register FERC notice, AEA web pages and the July 20th and 23rd press releases, the RRC site, the DNR notice and preliminary decision, the NSF award API, the UA FIF page and the UAA RAISE page. FERC's own news page returned HTTP 403.

claims.suggested_phrasing: was announced as keynote
claims.notes: The name 'Bryan Alexander' appears with this description. Delivery was not confirmed.

claims.claim: The symposium's Saturday sessions covered UA teaching, research funding and information security, and Sunday closed with a strategy session for the statewide AI advisory council.
claims.verbatim: Saturday's sessions turn to UA-specific questions - teaching, research funding, and information security - and Sunday closes with a strategy session for the statewide AI advisory council.
claims.suggested_phrasing: was scheduled to
claims.notes: The source uses dash characters here, which are rendered as hyphens in this verbatim. Do not quote this on a slide, because of the house no-dash rule.

S2 UA Statewide AI Symposium and UAA's NSF RAISE rural AI mini-grants

killed.claim: Names of the FERC commissioners who visited Bradley Lake, and the visit dates
killed.why: Neither is on the KTUU or WebCenter pages. ferc.gov/news-events/news returned HTTP 403, and AEA's press-release list has no release about the visit. Do not name commissioners.

killed.claim: Thayer quote 'We're going to have to turn off the lights and turn down the heat'
killed.why: It is not verbatim. The page reads 'We're going to have to turn off the lights and we're going to have to turn down the heat'. Use C18.

killed.claim: 22 attendees at the inaugural RAISE AI Solutions Consortium meeting, and the sectors represented
killed.why: The consortium page has no '22', 'inaugural', 'meeting' or 'attendees'. It only lists who may participate (industry, government, community organizations, UAA).

killed.claim: Air Force AI data center proposals closed June 29th
killed.why: The only fetched source (Air and Space Forces, April 11th) gives May 29 as the deadline. An extension was not verified.
It is not on any fetched page. HigherGov and SAM were not reachable without search.

killed.claim: Megawatt figures or minimum investment for the military data centers
killed.why: ADN and Air and Space Forces both state no MW or investment figures.

killed.claim: No final decision has been posted on ADL 422741
killed.why: An absence can't be proven from one notice page. It was replaced by C55, which says the decision is preliminary, with the status hedged.
This was imprecise. The notice says approximately 26 miles south of Deadhorse (C57).

killed.claim: The AEA Bradley Lake web page names the participating utilities
killed.why: The page does not name them. The utilities are sourced instead to AEA's July 20th release (C45).

killed.claim: The AEA Dixon Diversion page gives an energy figure
killed.why: The page has no energy percent or MWh. The energy figures are sourced to the FERC notice (C30) and the July 20th release (C41, C42).

killed.claim: The expansion increases Bradley Lake energy by 40 percent
killed.why: This is disputed. The FERC primary notice says approximately 38 percent, and AEA's own MWh figures give 38.3 percent. KTUU's 40 percent is water capacity, and AEA's 'more than 40 percent' does not match its own numbers. Use C30.

killed.claim: The RAISE mini-grant dollar amount per award
killed.why: It is not stated on the mini-grants page.

killed.claim: The symposium ran September 25 to 27 as a stated date range
killed.why: The AEDC page states only Friday September 25th explicitly and describes undated Saturday and Sunday sessions. Printing the 27th would rest on inference. Say 'Friday through Sunday'.
